title: 2001 HMMT February Algebra Problem 9
statement: Find the number of positive integer solutions to \(n^{x}+n^{y}=n^{z}\) with \(n^{z}<2001\).

solutions.text: If \(n=1\), the relation cannot hold, so assume otherwise. If \(x>y\), the left hand side factors as \(n^{y}\left(n^{x-y}+1\right)\) so \(n^{x-y}+1\) is a power of \(n\). But it leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by \(n\) and is greater than 1 , a contradiction. We reach a similar contradiction if \(y>x\). So \(y=x\) and \(2 n^{x}=n^{z}\), so 2 is a power of \(n\) and \(n=2\). So all solutions are of the form \(2^{x}+2^{x}=2^{x+1}\), which holds for all \(x .2^{x+1}<2001\) implies \(x<11\), so there are 10 solutions.
